title: CroCoNet: a framework for the quantitative comparison of gene regulatory networks across species.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 20343560 file listing via API (CC-BY-4.0): brain_dataset.zip 33.5 GB, validations.zip 8.5 GB, neural_differentiation_dataset.zip 4.4 GB, R package zip 28 MB, analysis scripts 0.6 MB. GEO GSE325993 metadata: single-cell CRISPRi (gene knockdown) subset with only POU5F1-perturbed and control cells, delivered as one RAW.tar; GSE326106 metadata: 10 long-read RNA-seq samples with GFF transcript models.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cell counts, donor counts (3 human, 2 gorilla, 4 macaque iPSC lines; 20 brain donors from 5 primates), network modules and conservation scores. None of the zips were opened: all exceed the 50 MB cap.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo open, CC-BY-4.0, and GEO open; checked via the APIs. Files are huge, though.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No outcome table exists. The only candidate targets (how conserved a network module is across species, or how a knockdown shifts expression) would have to be built from count matrices with CroCoNet itself. Judged from the file listing and paper.

a3_inputs_present.note: Count matrices are said to be inside the zips (paper text only, not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: UMI counts (unique molecule counts) are standard; not checked in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The natural unit is a regulator module or a species pair: a few hundred modules across 3–5 species, and the CRISPRi deposit covers one TF (transcription factor), POU5F1. Row count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The smallest dataset zip is 4.4 GB and the brain zip is 33.5 GB (checked on Zenodo). Building networks needs heavy single-cell processing.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without opening the zips.

a8_label_provenance.note: Module conservation scores are computed from the same expression data a model would use as input, so any label made from them is circular.

backbone.name: scGPT / Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would be the only fit

integration.join_key: Ensembl/GENCODE gene IDs (human gene build lifted over to apes)

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression from primate stem cells to predict which gene regulatory modules changed between species.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene-regulator modules inferred from single-cell RNA data of human, gorilla and macaque cells; number of modules unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a module has diverged between species, with the answer coming from CroCoNet's own conservation statistic, which is computed from the same data.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Evolutionary biologists could triage which regulators to test by knockdown, but the label isn't an independent measurement.

ml_idea: Predicting module divergence across primates. Not viable: the label is CroCoNet's own computed statistic, and the data are multi-GB raw-ish single-cell archives.

effort.compute_note: Only the Zenodo file sizes were checked; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Zenodo listing: the smallest dataset zip is 4.4 GB and there is no label table (already done).

verdict_reason: This is a methods paper for an R package (CroCoNet). Its data are 4.4–33.5 GB single-cell archives with no outcome column, and any label would be a statistic computed from the inputs (fails A2, A6 and A8).
